subject: Reducing the size of the INLA model object in memory

messages.author: fb2efbf28a86c396
messages.subject: Reducing the size of the INLA model object in memory
parts:
Hi INLA team,

I have recently fit a large INLA model, using the simplified Laplace approximation. After following the advice given on previous forum posts, I told INLA not to return posterior marginals and other irrelevant results in the model object to reduce the file size. I wish to simulate the posterior results and make predictions using inla.posterior.sample.

Unfortunately the model object is still huge (>80gb) and although I can read the model object in RAM, I cannot sample from it using the inla.posterior.sample function due to memory limits being reached. I am therefore wondering if there are any methods to reduce the result object size? For example, could I simply delete additional elements from the list before sampling? Alternatively, could I delete the stored integration grid for some of the variables (directly from the INLA result object) and sample using inla.posterior.sample on the remaining ones - repeating the process on a few variables at a time? If so, please could you provide me with a few pointers to help with the process?

Apologies if this post makes little sense - I can attempt to clarify things if need be.

Best,
Joe

Note - I have successfully fit the model using int.strategy = eb and with Gaussian approximations, but since I have successfully fit the larger Laplace version, I would like to use the results from this model in my paper.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Reducing the size of the INLA model object in memory

Hi Joe,

What sort of likelihood is it? (I’m guessing joint binomial/Gaussian, but if it’s Gaussian only there might be tricks). Also what are you using sampling to do? There might be a less expensive way.

(Also - I’m really interested in this work. Can you send the paper when you’re done?)

Best wishes,

Dan

messages.author: fb2efbf28a86c396
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Reducing the size of the INLA model object in memory
parts:
Hi Dan!

Happy New Year to you and the INLA team!

You are correct with it being a joint binomial/Gaussian, however there are an additional two Gaussian dummy variables to enable me to copy parts of the likelihood across the two models. This is why I suspect there is a lot of redundant junk stored in the INLA result file that can be removed.

I am sampling to generate posterior predictions at new locations, existing locations and to generate posterior credible intervals for these. I believe the latter would be especially difficult to, given only the summary statistics. Note I am not wanting to exclusively sample the predicted values (or linear predictors), but sometimes separate components of the linear predictors. I have also stored the config file to perform the sampling. I have noticed there are a LOT of Predictor and APredictor values sampled. Since I do not directly use these in my analysis, could I delete the config information relating to these?

Best Wishes,

Joe

P.S - I will absolutely send you the work :-)

I just wanted to check with you that you do not use a prediction stack. When you fit the data, you only use locations where you have observations, not locations where you just want to do predictions, correct?

PS: If you use prediction stack, the model is slow and large, this is why I am asking.

Kind regards,

messages.author: fb2efbf28a86c396
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Reducing the size of the INLA model object in memory
parts:
Hi Haakon,

You are correct that I have not formed a prediction stack when using the model. However, due to the model being a joint model I was required to form an additional stack for the second likelihood. Additionally, I needed to copy across two independent linear combinations of the hidden latent models across the two models. This required an additional two stacks to be formed for the dummy variables.

In total then, I have 4 data stacks.

After looking at the source code for the inla.posterior.sample, I am considering trying to delete the undesired result$misc$config$config elements and reduce the value of result$misc$config$nconfig accordingly. Does this sound sensible?

Best,
Joe

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Reducing the size of the INLA model object in memory
parts:
Hi Joe,

The nconfig is the number of integration points in theta-space when fitting the model. Rather than deleting, I would suggest rerunning the model with options that give fewer integration points. (Because it is safer, as you may do some coding errors otherwise) For example, if you run int.strategy="eb"  you only get 1 integration point.

If you want slightly more, you can see in
> ?control.inla
the
> dz
and
> diff.logdens
together they control the number of config you will get.

I would suggest trying int.strategy="ccd", diff.logdens=3

To know what values are reasonable to set for dz, we would need to ask Håvard.


Kind regards,
Haakon

Hi Haakon,

Thanks again for your speedy reply!

After considering your suggestions, I conclude that I cannot considerably reduce the file size. Thus I am left with two options:
  • Use the same computer - refit a reduced version of the model (e.g. with a smaller integration grid or eb method).
  • Use a bigger computer - use the fitted model object to sample from (will need more RAM).
I have decided to choose the second option.

Thanks again for all your help!
Joe
